title: Code-surgery bill of work — quick triage & followups
content:
Quick mental model: this is a single-pass triage for PRs that look like they need 'surgery' — small targeted fixes plus a bill-of-work for follow-ups.

Context: PR #2387 (model cache evictions) has a mix of small obvious fixes and a couple larger refactors that are 'nice-to-have' but high-risk. I want a runnable plan: what to land now, what to schedule, and how to observe regressions.

Top-level goals:
- keep latency SLOs intact (p50/p95)
- avoid large surface-area changes during high-traffic windows
- capture minimal repro and guardrails for each patch

Immediate quick fixes (ship these first, low-risk) — estimate: 1-2 dev-days total
- [ ] tighten null-check in cache_key() — currently returns None for empty meta; cause: observed NPE in logs (trace id 7a3f). Test: unit + small integration with mocked metadata. (owner: Kavita)
- [ ] add metric: cache_eviction_reason (enum: size, ttl, manual, collision). Emit in same code path as eviction. Backfill dashboards. (owner: Noah)
- [ ] revert accidental logging of full request payload in debug path — replace with truncated hash. (owner: Mira)

Medium work (schedule in sprint, needs review & tests) — estimate: 3-6 dev-days
- [ ] decouple eviction policy from global state: pull policy into EvictionPolicy object with interface (shouldEvict, recordAccess). Rationale: makes unit testing deterministic; avoids global lock contention. Risks: interface ripple to two callers. Rollout: feature flag behind runtime.eviction_refactor. (tests: unit + perf microbench)
- [ ] tighten threading model in cache: convert a few non-atomic counters to atomic/lock. Risk: potential perf regression if naive. Bench plan: run locust scenario (1000 rps synthetic) and compare ops/sec on dedicated test infra.

Large refactor / aspirational (put into backlog, design doc required)
- [ ] rewrite cache to use segmented shards keyed by model_id so eviction scopes are smaller and contention reduced. This is basically a migration and needs rollout plan and data migration. Put behind an opt-in cluster flag and canary.

Rollback & mitigation plan (for any shipped fix that causes regression)
- In hosted: be ready to toggle runtime.eviction_refactor=false to rollback medium change. Ensure config push has no downtime.
- If small fix causes increased error rate: hotfix branch with revert and quick patch to restore previous behavior.

Observability checklist (must be done before we consider rolling anything)
- [ ] dashboard: p50/p95 latency for inference route (per model variant) with baseline and change window.
- [ ] dashboard: cache_hit_rate, cache_eviction_rate, cache_eviction_reason (new metric).
- [ ] error rate by endpoint and trace ids — be able to filter to requests that experienced eviction concurrently.
- [ ] add a debug-level sample of 1/1000 requests that log minimal context (model_id, seq_len, cache_key_hash) to correlate with traces.

Test matrix (minimal required)
- unit tests for cache_key edge cases (empty meta, unicode keys, very long strings)
- concurrency test: spawn 32 threads hitting same model_id, assert no data race (run with TSAN / race detector locally)
- perf microbench: measure avg token generation latency with and without the medium patch on same hardware; keep delta < 5% for p50 and p95.

Notes-to-self / reviewer prompts (what I want reviewers to pay attention to)
- is the new metric name clear and usable for dashboards? (cache_eviction_reason vs cache_eviction_cause)
- any simpler way to avoid global state besides the EvictionPolicy wrapper? I tried an approach using function-local singletons but that made tests brittle.
- sanity-check the feature-flag plumbing; does the flag flip require worker restart or is it dynamic? If dynamic, are there race possibilities?

Open questions / TODOs
- [ ] ask infra whether the config push can be atomic (no partial rollouts) — ping @infra on Slack
- [ ] check with SRE whether 1/1000 debug sampling is acceptable retention-wise
- [ ] estimate cost of segmented-shard migration (ops time + perf test time) — rough ballpark: 2 engineers x 2 weeks

Commit message guidance for quick fixes
- "cache: avoid returning None from cache_key when meta empty; add unit test"
- "telemetry: add cache_eviction_reason metric; increment on each eviction"
- "logging: truncate request payload before debug log to avoid PII"

Mini retrospective after landing (to fill after deploy)
- Did p95 latency change? (number)
- Did cache hit rate improve or regress? (number)
- Any new alerts fired? Which ones and why?

This doc is a scratchpad; refine into a PR checklist and attach to PR description before requesting review. Keep items idempotent and small — the goal is predictable, observable changes, and to avoid large refactors landing mid-traffic.
